summary: Developed with big wave rider Ben Wilson, the Fuse is Slingshot's dedicated wave weapon. Deep drift bridle keeps it in the pocket down the line, clean depower for slack on the face, and instant redirect for fast turns and downloops. Purpose-built for strapless surfing.

sources.summary: Dedicated wave riders are impressed by the deep drift and clean depower. Ben Wilson's input shows.
Strong early reviews from wave riders. The drift is class-leading and the redirect is lightning fast.

reviews.full_transcript: [Music] Heat. Hey, Heat. [Music] Heat. [Music] Welcome to the gliten.tv review of the new Slingshot Fuse. The Wave model is now called Fuse, has been completely redesigned and has nothing in common with the old SST. On the new Fuse, the front tube is suspended at four points and the bridal features a pulley. The steering lines are of course connected directly to the tip and there are three different options to further adjust bar pressure and turning speed to your personal preference. The bridal is overall quite short, so you only need line deflectors at the end of the front tube. The middle cross struts have no line deflectors. Inflation and deflation are handled via a modern SUP valve and the one pump system is very short and only slightly angled. The material of the front tube is a high strength Dron with rectangular reinforcement from polyester threads. The front tube is sealed here with a simple keedar seam which is doubled and simply stitched from the inside. A quadruple riptop material is used here for the canopy. And in the areas of the trailing edge as well as the front frame, that is the front panel support of the leading edge, we have a heavy dacron material. And of course, not to be forgotten, there are also two battens on each side to prevent any flapping. The struts are each attached to the canopy with a single seam which is doubled and glued from the inside. And here again is the heavier fabric strip that forms the transition from the front tube to the canopy. [Music] We tested this kite for you in 7 and 9 square meters. Of course, with the directional board using different models here and also when flying the kite during the planing process, it was very noticeable that the canopy remains very stable even when starting in very critical spots. It shows no tendency for front or back stall and can be easily controlled here. And with a gentle sine wave, which you can continue a bit to accelerate the kite and release as much energy as possible, the airflow attaches to the kite very quickly. And as soon as you are flying steadily, we have an extremely consistent forward drive here. [Music] The rather flat profile with its very small leading edge diameter allows for a very sharp angle against the wind. Accordingly, it's very easy to get back to the lineup with this kite. So, riding up wind with the fuse is really as easy as it gets. The canopy effortlessly catches air at the edge of the wind window, even without corrections, delivering excellent performance. One of the most important aspects of a kite is of course always the bar feeling, especially with a wave kite. The fuse is truly direct and absolutely precise. And it also works well with little line tension. With a steered style, it follows very quickly and willingly in the individual turns. And even when drifting, it remains responsive at all times. All of this is accompanied by light holding and steering forces. You always get good feedback about the kite's position in the wind window. If you're used to very firm and strong bar forces, it takes a second or two to get used to the slightly different timing and feel here, but you adapt to this tuning very quickly. The basic pull of the fuse is not particularly strong. It's in the medium to low range here. It thrives on a mix of basic pull and a rather high flight speed. Here we have a wave kite that really wants to be moved and positioned precisely. And this is where the positive elements like the slightly lighter bar forces come together beautifully in this combination. All in all, this results in a homogeneous and very agile overall impression because the fuse also intuitively positions itself in the right spot. And even when you move it at a high flight speed, it doesn't deliver excessive power spikes that would knock you off the board when riding strapless. And if we look at the flight pattern, meaning the turning radi and the turning speed as well here, it moves in medium to tight radi. And the overall flight behavior is always smooth and consistent. To get the fuse to even start to spin out, you really have to steer very hard with a lot of line tension. And here too, the medium to high flight speed in the turns fits very harmoniously with the overall power delivery and the rest of the kite's behavior. It's also worth mentioning again that even when it's positioned far at the edge of the wind window or heavily depowered, it still remains responsive to steering. [Music] Anyone who wants to use the new Fuse for strapless freestyle jumping will get consistently good performance here. There are definitely a few kites on the market that offer even more boost and are a bit easier to find the sweet spot with, especially the models that generally have more bar pressure are definitely a bit easier in this regard. But after a short adjustment period, you can quickly get comfortable with the Fuse as well. All in all, it can be said that the Fuse V1 is a really nice and stable wave kite that doesn't take long to get used to since it is fundamentally well balanced in all areas. Especially when it truly comes to strapless surfing or strapless freestyle, there's always a little bit of a significant dilemma about precisely what you actually and truly want to achieve. Do you want a bit more boost, meaning a more explosive power delivery, or do you prefer a kite that always works with absolutely smooth and even power distribution? here. It really hits the sweet spot right in the middle, but it does lean a few% more towards the softer and more even power delivery. Nevertheless, as already mentioned, when it comes to jumping, you can definitely achieve good performance here. The consistently light to medium bar pressure is of course immediately appealing to lighter riders, but even heavier riders have no problem getting enough power out of the fuse. And the gliding characteristics and power during gliding are truly more than sufficient. In terms of its overall tuning, it feels noticeably fresher and more modern compared to the previous model. And let's take another look at the different styles. Whether we want to fly with quick steering or in a drifting manner. Here too, the Fuse has found a nice middle ground. It's fast enough to provide plenty of energy for those who want to ride longer turns or use straps. It complements this with a medium to high flight speed. And when drifting, it's almost self-sufficient positioning naturally helps it. If you make only slight corrections, it helps with its drift. And it can also hold its position very nicely for a long time with low line tension. This makes it very attractive for pure strapless surfers because as mentioned it doesn't deliver any unwanted power spikes in between. The build quality of this wave kite is as is typical for slingshot absolutely solid and the materials which are now a bit more modern here are also very well matched. So when you think about durability the fund should last a long time. The price of the fuse is €1,499 for the seven square meter size, which considering today's overall price situation seems realistic to us. From our perspective, the Fuse V1 is definitely highly recommended for the kite surfing sector. No matter which style you personally prefer, [Music]
reviews.summary: Gleiten tv tested the Fuse in 7 and 9m sizes and praised its extremely precise, direct steering with light bar forces that remain responsive even when drifting or heavily depowered. They highlighted its smooth, spike-free power delivery as ideal for strapless surfing, and noted solid upwind ability. The main trade-off flagged is that boost-seekers will find better options elsewhere, and lighter bar pressure requires brief acclimatization.

structured_review.summary: The Slingshot Fuse 2026 is a purpose-built wave kite that delivers smooth, consistent power with light-to-medium bar pressure and a clean drift. It excels at strapless surfing with responsive, precise steering even with minimal line tension. The main caveat is its lean toward even power delivery over explosive boost, making it a secondary choice for riders who prioritize air time.
pros: Extremely precise and direct steering even with low line tension
Excellent drift — holds position naturally with minimal input and no unwanted power spikes
Clean, consistent power delivery without sudden surges that would unbalance a strapless rider
Very good upwind performance thanks to flat profile and small leading edge diameter
Remains stable and steerable even when heavily depowered or at the edge of the wind window
Solid build quality with modern materials including Dron front tube and quadruple ripstop canopy
cons: Basic pull is in the medium-to-low range — not a big boost kite
Lighter bar pressure requires a short adjustment period for riders used to firmer, more high-pressure setups
Finding the sweet spot for jumping takes more effort compared to kites with higher bar pressure
One-pump system is described as very short and only slightly angled — a minor ergonomic inconvenience
structured_review.best_for: Strapless wave surfers who want smooth, drift-friendly power delivery, precise steering, and reliable upwind performance across different turn styles.
structured_review.not_for: Riders who prioritize explosive boost and high bar pressure for big air or strapless freestyle jumping.
structured_review.rec_blurb: Drifts like a dream — the strapless surfer's precision tool with zero nasty surprises.
